---
title: "Stage 0 — map the protocol to ICH M11"
---

A protocol written for people, read against a structure written for machines. Nothing is
changed yet; this stage only finds out what the protocol does and does not say.

## What this is

ICH M11 is a template for the clinical trial protocol: fourteen sections, and in the merged
electronic version 303 data elements, 216 of them Required, each carrying a CDISC code.
Mapping means deciding, element by element, which piece of the existing protocol answers it —
and recording the ones nothing answers.

## What you do

Read the source protocol against the element list and write the mapping down. The output is a
table, not an edit: element, where it is satisfied, or *absent*.

The absences are the interesting half, so record them with the same care as the matches.

## What you should see

A mapping document, and a count of required elements the protocol does not supply.

For TORIVA that count is 25, across six objectives.

## What to look out for

**Everything M11 wants usually exists somewhere — it is just in the wrong document.** M11
§3.1.1 requires the estimand *in the protocol*, and five of its seven required elements are
ICH E9(R1) estimand attributes. TORIVA defers all five to the SAP. Nothing was missing from
the study; it was misplaced, and only a structured reading made that countable.

Resist fixing anything here. The temptation to correct the protocol while mapping it is
strong, and it destroys the measurement — you can no longer say what the protocol did say.
